groups.title: Shape the code and its docs
Make plugins, and see what they cost

but-first-planning.cue: turn an idea into a spec, a backlog, and built issues
but-first-planning.how: Three phases, each leaving files in a workspace: write and sharpen a spec, decompose it into a backlog, then build that backlog one issue at a time, test-first. The project's workspace is `.agents/plan/`, which `spec-init` scaffolds the first time; a feature or a long task gets its own, `.agents/plans/<name>/`, made when you ask for its spec.

uses.want: be questioned on a goal until nothing about it is left unsaid
write or extend the spec for a project or a feature
break a finished spec into epics, sprints, and issues
find the next unblocked issue of the plan

agent-works.cue: run several tasks at once, each in its own session
agent-works.how: The session becomes the orchestrator: it turns a goal into cards on a kanban board, asks before starting anything, has a subagent build each card in its own worktree (or a child session, when you ask for sessions), and reviews what comes back. It also keeps a repo's agent-facing files in one place under `.agents/`.

uses.want: build a goal bigger than one change, or resume a round
see what is on the board, add to it, or move a card
set a repository up for agent work
find out why agent files have bloated, or what the machine lacks

agentic-teamwork.cue: set up, check, or ship a repo the team's way
agentic-teamwork.how: Most of it runs unasked: hooks judge commits and pushes against the team's git conventions. What a person starts by name is the setup, the audit, and the two ends of landing work.

uses.want: put a new repo on the team conventions before any code is written
check the repo against the conventions and repair what drifted
commit the work in hand and open its pull or merge request
merge a reviewed request once its checks are green

code-diet.cue: keep new code small, and cut what is not needed
code-diet.how: On any coding task the agent takes the simplest rung that works, checks what already exists before building, and marks what it defers as debt. A person asks for the review or the debt inventory.

uses.want: hunt over-engineering in the working diff before a request
check what already exists before building something
list every deferred shortcut and whether it still holds
note what this work built that another project could use

codebase-optimizer.cue: restructure a codebase that has grown messy
codebase-optimizer.how: It works in stages on a branch, each one checked by the repo's own tests and reverted when they go red: organize the tree, split the god-files, deepen shallow modules.

uses.want: the whole sweep, stage by stage
reorganize a sprawling file tree and nothing else
find shallow modules and leaky seams and nothing else

docs-parity.cue: keep user docs level with the code
docs-parity.how: Pages, screenshots, and the nav move in the same change as the code they describe; a Stop check and CI say when they did not.

uses.want: bring the docs level with a change before it is committed
find out whether the whole docs set is current
cut a README down to what a newcomer needs
adopt the docs checks in a repo

system-map.cue: keep a diagram of the system that the code checks
system-map.how: `@system` annotations in the code become a committed map that is checked against the imports and drawn as a frame on a Miro board, with a lint before publishing and a live check after.

uses.want: give a repo a system map generated from its code
bring the map and its board level with a code change
draw or update a diagram on Miro
set up the browser the live Miro check drives

picture-this.cue: draw how something works as an animated figure
picture-this.how: From a description or a feature in a codebase it finds the lens, models the subject, drafts three views, refines one, and delivers a React component plus stills for a README.

uses.want: turn a system, a mechanism, or an idea into a figure
retake a figure's stills, strip, or GIF for a README

perceptual-loop.cue: check work judged by eye or ear
perceptual-loop.how: The session writes down what will prove a change, renders a few reproducible shots before and after, gates the numbers against the last accepted run, and looks at the picture before calling it done. Questions of taste wait for the person on one review page.

uses.want: start any change to how something looks, moves, or sounds
set a project up so it can render a shot on command
check an animation, a transition, or a clip
check a sound, or a sound against its picture

write-like-me.cue: write in your own voice, and catch AI tells
write-like-me.how: A calibrated profile of how the person writes, applied to prose a human will read, with hooks that learn from style feedback.

uses.want: build or rebuild the voice profile
draft something in their voice
check a draft for AI-writing tells
see or undo what the learning loop changed

workflow-studio.cue: build a Claude Code workflow, by canvas or by hand
workflow-studio.how: A node editor in the browser for dynamic workflows, and the rules for writing the same scripts and graphs by hand.

uses.want: open the visual editor
write or change a workflow script or its graph directly

plugin-workbench.cue: make, score, or fix a plugin or its skills
plugin-workbench.how: One rubric serves all of it: a new plugin is scaffolded against it, as a skill per job or as areas with routes and one skill to type; an existing one is scored into a scorecard with a verdict; and the fixes are applied in the order of the points each is worth.

uses.want: make a new plugin, or wrap skills and scripts they already have
raise an existing plugin's score
score a plugin and get a scorecard with a verdict
reinstall a marketplace checkout from the working tree

context-doctor.cue: see what a session's agent was actually given
context-doctor.how: It reads a session's transcript back: each hook's output and who saw it, the skill listing, the rule files, the size of every request, and what each compaction kept or lost. Then it names what went wrong, with the fix for each.

uses.want: find out why a session ignored a rule or forgot its instructions
see what entered an agent's context, and from which area
